topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning objectives, tumor progression model, and the framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Sustained proliferative signaling and growth factor independence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase, Wnt, and downstream signaling cascades disrupt normal growth control to drive continuous cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation arrest in hematological and epithelial cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how genetic alterations block terminal cellular differentiation across leukemias and colorectal carcinomas to sustain precursor cell expansion.

topics.label: Evasion of programmed cell death and apoptosis regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how cancer cells resist apoptosis through mutations impairing the p53 tumor suppressor pathway and shifting the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance, senescence bypass, and cellular immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit and normal p53-mediated senescence through telomerase activation to achieve replicative immortality.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolite signaling in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells rewire metabolic pathways toward aerobic glycolysis and how metabolic enzyme mutations alter the epigenome to promote tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and vascular supply
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the requirement for new blood vessel formation to overcome diffusion limits, its timing during progression, and the balance between pro- and anti-angiogenic signals.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and barriers of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the multistep cascade of metastatic dissemination, clinical monitoring methods, and the genetic and microenvironmental factors governing secondary site colonization.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with final remarks on unifying cancer hallmarks, recommended reading, and practical session information.
